issue_context.title: duckdb_param_type returns DUCKDB_TYPE_INVALID for VARCHAR params (only)
issue_context.body:
### What happens?

The C API function `duckdb_param_type`, when called for a parameter of type VARCHAR, returns DUCKDB_TYPE_INVALID.

### To Reproduce

Here's a test case that fails:

```c
TEST_CASE("Test duckdb_param_type for VARCHAR", "[capi]") {
	duckdb_database db;
	duckdb_connection conn;
	duckdb_prepared_statement stmt;

	REQUIRE(duckdb_open("", &db) == DuckDBSuccess);
	REQUIRE(duckdb_connect(db, &conn) == DuckDBSuccess);
	REQUIRE(duckdb_prepare(conn, "select ?", &stmt) == DuckDBSuccess);

	REQUIRE(duckdb_bind_varchar(stmt, 1, "a") == DuckDBSuccess);

	REQUIRE(duckdb_param_type(stmt, 1) == DUCKDB_TYPE_VARCHAR);
}
```

It fails on the final REQUIRE with `0 == 17`.

### OS:

Mac OS X 

### DuckDB Version:

main branch

### DuckDB Client:

C API

### Hardware:

Apple M2 Max

### Full Name:

Jeff Raymakers

comments:
I traced this down to the `return_type` of the `BoundParameterData` having the value `LogicalTypeId::STRING_LITERAL` instead of `LogicalTypeId::VARCHAR`. This is due to the special case in [BoundParameterData::GetDefaultType](https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/blob/2d530ad3650f2f17bd1d2afdb1ea44e548227918/src/include/duckdb/planner/expression/bound_parameter_data.hpp#L44). (`BoundParameterData` is constructed in a way that calls `GetDefaultType` in `duckdb_bind_value`.)

I'm not sure what the right fix is. Is it correct that the bound parameter data has STRING_LITERAL? If so, then perhaps a special check needs to be added to `duckdb_param_logical_type`, so it doesn't create a `LogicalType` with STRING_LITERAL. Or perhaps it's valid for `duckdb_param_type` to return STRING_LITERAL, in which case that type needs to be added to the C API and a case needs to be added to `ConvertCPPTypeToC`.

review_comments:
Is it necessary to add STRING_LITERAL? Can't we just return VARCHAR?
I was under the impression that STRING_LITERAL is only relevant to the binder, exposing that detail to users feels unnecessary?

Hmm, I don't think the C++ API is a good argument because that is not guaranteed to be stable.
But the behavior for string literals is different than varchar, I believe they auto cast to other types(?)

It's a little strange to me that `bind_varchar` results in a string literal
I guess it's emulating this query example
```sql
D prepare p1 as select [21, $1, 42];
D execute p1('200');
┌─────────────────────────────┐
│ main.list_value(21, $1, 42) │
│           int32[]           │
├─────────────────────────────┤
│ [21, 200, 42]               │
└─────────────────────────────┘
```

But `duckdb_bind_varchar` sounds kind of like this is expected instead
```sql
D execute p1('200'::VARCHAR);
Binder Error:
Cannot create a list of types INTEGER_LITERAL and VARCHAR - an explicit cast is required
```
While we're on the topic, `INTEGER_LITERAL` should also be handled with whatever path ends up being taken

The C API is also used in situations where binding matters (e.g. binding of functions) - so I think adding the enum here makes sense. `STRING_LITERAL` can be anything while `VARCHAR` can only be text, so there is value in having both options also in this scenario.
Alright, then I think `INTEGER_LITERAL` should also be covered?
Yes sounds good, I'll add it to this PR.
